title: Anchoring the Course Span of a Visit Referral Lengthening
content:
When an In-Group Specialist Referral, an HMO Specialist Referral, an Out-of-Network Referral or a Physical Therapy Episode Authorization (Referrals & Prior Authorizations) is lengthened, the anchor of the course span follows the referral's status:

1. **Exhausted referral.** The span runs from the handling date, so the anchored span is the span less the days from the handling date to the valid-through date.
2. **Approved referral close to its end.** For an approved referral with fewer days left to the valid-through date than the type's extension request lead days, the span runs from the handling date plus those lead days, so the anchored span is the span plus the lead days less the days left.
3. **Any other referral.** The span runs from the valid-through date, and the anchored span is the span itself.

The anchored span is a count of calendar days that goes into the course validity days of the lengthening.

The **days left** are the calendar days from the handling date to the valid-through date. The type's extension request lead days are 14 for the In-Group Specialist Referral, 10 for the HMO Specialist Referral, 10 for the Out-of-Network Referral and 7 for the Physical Therapy Episode Authorization. "Fewer than" is strict: days left equal to the lead days fall under clause 3.

## Worked cases (hypothetical referrals)

| Status | Span | Days left | Lead days | Clause | Anchored span |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| exhausted | 114 | 20 | 14 | 1 | 114 less 20: 94 |
| approved | 56 | 6 | 10 | 2 | 56 plus 10 less 6: 60 |
| approved | 56 | 10 | 10 | 3 | 56 |
| approved | 56 | 30 | 7 | 3 | 56 |

In the first case the span of 114 days measured from the handling date ends 94 days after the valid-through date, which lies 20 days ahead.
